steps: Make the coefficients of one variable the same by multiplying
Add or subtract the equations to eliminate one variable
Solve for the remaining variable, then substitute back to find the other
method_card.title: How to Solve Simultaneous Equations (Linear)
method_card.content:
Simultaneous equations are two (or more) equations that are true at the same time. The solution is the pair of values that satisfies both equations.

Elimination method: Make the coefficients of one variable equal, then add or subtract the equations to eliminate that variable. Solve for the remaining variable, then substitute back.

Substitution method: Rearrange one equation to make one variable the subject, then substitute into the other equation.

Always check your answer by substituting both values into both original equations.
method_card.example:
Solve \(2x + 3y = 12\) and \(5x - 3y = 9\)

Step 1: y-coefficients are already +3 and -3

Step 2: Add equations: \(7x = 21\), so \(x = 3\)

Step 3: Substitute into (1): \(6 + 3y = 12\), so \(y = 2\)

Check in (2): \(15 - 6 = 9\) \(\checkmark\)

steps: Sometimes no single multiplication works. Multiply BOTH equations to a common target: \(5y\) and \(3y\) both reach \(15y\) with \(\times 3\) and \(\times 5\).
Everything else is the same: same signs subtract, opposite signs add, substitute back, check.
Prefer rearranging? Substitution also works: make a letter the subject and put it into the other equation. Either method gets full marks.
gold.title: Gold: multiply both equations

steps: You need the one pair of values, an \(x\) AND a \(y\), that fits both equations. In bronze a matching pair is already there (like \(+y\) in both).
Same Signs Subtract: subtract one equation from the other, right-hand sides too, and the matched letter vanishes. Opposite signs (\(+y\) and \(-y\))? Add instead.
Solve the one-letter equation that is left, then substitute your value into the easier original equation to find the other letter.
